When do open weights catch up?

A least-squares fit through each class’s record-setting releases over the last 24 months, extended forward. Two different questions: when an open class reaches the score the frontier holds today, and whether the open trend is gaining on the frontier trend at all. Both a linear and a quadratic fit are shown for every class; switch models to see how much the answer depends on that choice.

Intelligence Index

On its current trend, the soonest to reach today’s frontier score of 65.7 is Data-center open weights, around Feb 2027 — 5 months from now.

Whether any class is gaining on the frontier is a different question, and this model cannot answer it: every slope difference sits inside its own standard error, so the gap is best read as holding roughly constant.

On its current trend, the soonest to reach today’s frontier score of 65.7 is Data-center open weights, around Oct 2026 — 1 month from now.

Looking further out, Data-center open weights is gaining on the frontier fast enough that the two trends meet around Apr 2027. Quadratic fits extrapolate acceleration, so they land earlier than the linear ones — and diverge fast past the fitted window.

Read these as arithmetic, not forecasts. Both models are straight-line and curved fits through a short, noisy history of a fast-moving field, and the releases they fit are by construction the maxima of their class. A quadratic always fits at least as well as a linear one, so the R² columns are not a fair contest on their own — the F-test beside the quadratic R² is what says whether the curvature earns its extra parameter. The “reaches” column is the sturdier of the two estimates: it depends on one curve. The gap column depends on the difference of two curves, which is far noisier — under the linear model, where that difference does not clear twice its standard error, no crossing date is quoted.

How the classes are drawn

Split by where the weights can actually run. The two consumer tiers are cumulative — < 120B parameters includes everything in “27B and under”, because it answers the question “what is the best model I can run within this budget?” Where both tiers share a record holder their lines coincide and the point is annotated once.

Frontier

Closed-weight models served only by API. The ceiling of what exists.

65.7Claude Fable 5.1 · Sep 2026

Data-center open weights

Downloadable weights of 120B parameters or more — the large mixture-of-experts releases that need a multi-GPU node to serve.

59.7Kimi K3 · Jul 2026

< 120B parameters

Open weights small enough for a single high-memory accelerator or a 128 GB workstation.

52.0Qwen3.8 27B · Aug 2026

27B and under

The single-GPU tier — open weights that fit on one prosumer card. Models branded "27B" report 27.8B parameters, so the bound sits just above 27 to admit them; set maxParams to 27 for a strict cutoff.
